text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Ruling coalition outvotes opposition in parliament to pass health insurance reform law which will mean higher contributions from patients.
- German steel makers Krupp and larger rival Thyssen hold talks over a possible joint steel company, designed to avert Krupp's hostile takeover.

- German parliament retrospectively ratifies a spectacular rescue operation by German troops last Friday to get Germans and other nationals out of Albania as the Balkan country slid further into chaos.

- Bavaria begins slaughter of 3,000 imported cattle from Britain and Switzerland, following new scare over mad cow disease which prompted states to agree to kill all cattle imported from the two countries.

- Opposition Social Democrat (SPD) parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping says negotiations between SPD and the ruling coalition on tax reform proposals cannot continue until Chancellor Helmut Kohl agrees to talk to SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine.
- German Finance Ministry says the number of unemployed in Germany should sink faster in spring than is usual for theis time of year, when the effects of the harsh winter receed.
HANDELSBLATT

- Despite talks between Krupp and Thyssen over linking up steel activities, Krupp still interested in taking full control of its larger rival and has secured a 15 billion mark credit line from banks to do so, according to banking sources.
- Bayerische Vereinsbank chairman Albrecht Schmidt criticises Bonn government for not converting government debt to euros.
- Lower house of parliament overturns rejection of the upper house of unemployment benefit reform meaning new rules can come into effect, including a measures to fight fraudulent claims.
- Luxury carmaker BMW AG says expects to pay a dividend of 15 marks per ordinary share in 1996, up from 13.50 marks the year before.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Ruling coalition pushes health insurance reform through parliament which will mean higher contributions by patients for prescription drugs and dental treatment.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel, leader of the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) warns rival Bavaria premier Edmund Stoiber against challenging him for the leadership.
- Ruling coalition offers SPD possible meeting times for new tax talks during the Easter holiday.
DIE WELT
- Guido Westerwelle, general secretary of junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) says tax reform talks between coaltion and opposition SPD have failed.
- Krupp and Thyssen begin discussions over forming a joint steel company.
- Parliament agrees on higher contributions by patients to the cost of drugs, travel and hospital visits.
